business-e2e-context

Bunkai E2E map

How people use Bunkai TMS end to end: personas from the roles the code recognises, journeys traced through routes, then the feature catalog. Paths are relative to ../upex-bunkai-tms; route: names an app route.

Overview

Bunkai is used by QA teams inside a workspace. Everyone in a workspace has one role; the role decides what they can change, and a Personal Access Token lets agents and CI act as their owner through the same API. The UI hides controls by role, but the real gate is the API and Row Level Security, so a role check must be tested at the API, not only in the UI.

Role hierarchy and permission matrix

viewer < member < admin < owner (SQL helpers bunkai_is_workspace_member, bunkai_can_write_workspace, bunkai_is_workspace_admin, bunkai_is_workspace_owner; soft-deleted workspaces excluded).

Top journeys

  • Manual run (journey-manual-run): the daily work and the source of every metric; highest data risk.
  • Authoring (journey-authoring): the traceability rule (ATC needs a story and an AC) is enforced here.
  • Agent or CI run (journey-agent-ci-run): the product's differentiator; same endpoints, token auth.
  • Upgrade (journey-upgrade-billing): the only path where money changes hands.
  • Sign up and onboarding (journey-signup-onboarding): first impression; blocked for automation by the email OTP.

Journeysagent-ci-run

Journey: sign up and first project

Entry: /login (or any protected URL, which redirects to /login?next=…).

  1. Email-first form asks POST /api/v1/auth/check-email whether the account exists and is confirmed.
  2. New account: POST /auth/signup (email ≤254, password 8–128) answers 202 pending_confirmation; duplicate email is 409 "An account with that email already exists."
  3. External step: a 6-digit OTP arrives by email and is submitted to /auth/confirm. Resend failure: "Could not resend the verification code. Please check your details and try again."
  4. Alternatives: password sign-in, magic link (login only, external email), GitHub or Google OAuth (external provider).
  5. First login lands on /onboarding: create a workspace (name 1–80, slug 3–40 lowercase, not reserved; collision 409).
  6. Create the first project (/projects/new); community allows 3 projects.

Failure points: rate limit 429 on auth endpoints; a reserved or taken slug; the 4th community project (45700). Automation: start from a pre-confirmed account (ADR-0027); the OTP and OAuth steps are not automatable.

Data and API: business-data-context flow-workspace-onboarding; business-api-context group-auth, group-workspaces.

Journey: author from story to Test

  1. Project explorer (/projects/[slug]): create a module (name 2–80).
  2. Add a user story to the module (title 3–200, description ≤50,000 bytes; Jira key format ABC-123).
  3. Add acceptance criteria in the panel; the story can become ready_to_test only with at least one active AC.
  4. Create an ATC (/atcs/new): title 3–200, layer, at least one step, each step ≤2048 bytes, up to 10 tags, at least one linked AC of the same story.
  5. Build a Test (/tests/new): title 1–200, ordered ATC chain of at least one ATC, up to 20 tags.

Branches: archived parent blocks edits (45025); removing the last AC drops the story to draft; viewers see no create buttons. Data: flow-authoring, entity-atc. API: group-projects-modules, group-stories-ac, group-atcs, group-tests.

Journey: execute a manual run

  1. Test detail page → Start run (POST /api/v1/runs) with an environment.
  2. Runner (/projects/[slug]/runs/[runId], data-testid="runner-view"): mark each step passed, failed or blocked, with an optional note (≤2000) and evidence link (http/https). Error: "Could not mark this step."
  3. Attach screenshots to a step (PNG, JPEG, WebP; 10 MiB each, 10 per step).
  4. On a failed step, file a bug (title 5–200, severity P1–P4, up to 10 evidence links); the runner shows the linked bug banner.
  5. Finish: choose the verdict (runner-finish-verdict-passed / -failed); missing verdict: "Select a final verdict of passed or failed to finish the run." Or abort with a reason of 3–500 characters.

Failure points: no executable steps (45202, 422); invalid environment (45201); marking or finishing a closed run (409); a run left open is auto-aborted after 4 hours of inactivity. Silent risk: the verdict is chosen by the person, so a run with failed steps can be finished as passed. Data: flow-manual-run, state-runs. API: group-runs, group-bugs.

Journey: triage bugs

  1. Bugs list (/projects/[slug]/bugs); viewers cannot create.
  2. Assign or reassign to an active non-viewer member (/bugs/{id}/assign).
  3. Move status one step forward (/bugs/{id}/status): open → in_progress → resolved → closed. Skipping: "A bug must move to '<next>' first."; backward: "A bug's status cannot move backward."
  4. Watch the defect heatmap per module (/bugs/heatmap?window=).

No reopen exists: a regression after closed needs a new bug. Data: flow-bug-lifecycle, state-bugs. API: group-bugs.

Journey: plan, sign off and track a release

  1. Create a test plan (name 1–100, description ≤500, goal ≤100) and add Tests of the same project.
  2. Execute the plan's Tests (manual or automated runs).
  3. Close the plan with a verdict and summary (≤4000). A closed plan cannot be edited: "This test plan is closed and can no longer be edited." Reopen clears the verdict.
  4. Create a milestone (name 1–100, target date today to +5 years) and attach up to 50 plans; readiness = closed plans / attached plans.

Data: flow-test-plan-milestone. API: group-test-plans-milestones.

Journey: invite a teammate

  1. Admin or owner opens members (/workspaces/[id]/members) and invites an email (≤254) as viewer, member or admin.
  2. External step: the invite email; the link opens /invites/accept?token=….
  3. Signed out: redirect to /login?next=/invites/accept?token=…; then accept (POST /api/v1/invites/accept). Error: "Could not accept invite."
  4. Admins can revoke or resend (resend rotates the token).

Failure points: expired after 7 days, revoked, already member with an equal or higher role. Data: flow-membership. API: group-members-invites.

Journey: upgrade to Cloud

  1. Owner opens /settings/billing/upgrade (owner-only page).
  2. Checkout: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout creates a Stripe session.
  3. External step: Stripe hosted checkout. Success returns to /settings/billing?upgraded=1; cancel returns to /settings/billing/upgrade?checkout=canceled and calls the cancel endpoint.
  4. The plan changes only when the Stripe webhook arrives with payment paid; the return URL alone changes nothing.

Money changes hands here. Failure points: processor not configured (503 payment_processor_unavailable), a second open checkout, a delayed webhook (page shows the old plan). Data: flow-billing-upgrade. API: group-billing.

Journey: import stories from Jira

  1. Admin connects Jira in settings (site, email, API token).
  2. In a project, "Import from Jira" (POST /api/v1/imports); the dialog polls GET /api/v1/imports/{jobId}.
  3. Stories and ACs land in modules matching Jira components, else an Inbox module.

Non-admins see a "not connected" message that differs by role. External dependency: a real Jira site. Data: flow-jira-import. API: group-jira-imports.

Journey: delete and restore a workspace

  1. Owner deletes from /settings/workspaces (DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}); access stops at once.
  2. External step: the restore email links to /workspaces/[id]/restore (public route).
  3. Signed out: redirect to login, then restore (POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/restore, owner, browser session only). Error: "Could not restore the workspace."
  4. After 30 days the workspace is purged and cannot be restored.

Destructive: never run against a shared workspace. Data: flow-workspace-deletion. API: group-data-lifecycle.

Journey: agent or CI run through the API

  1. Get a token: from /settings/tokens (name, at least one scope, expiry 30/90/365 days in the UI) or headless POST /api/v1/auth/signin, which returns a session and a fresh PAT.
  2. Streamed: create the run (executor_mode agent or ci), mark steps, finish; idle 60 minutes = auto-aborted.
  3. One-shot: POST /api/v1/runs/submissions with verdict and all step results; must agree (45235).
  4. Results appear in run history and metrics exactly like manual runs; the executor gets the finish notification.

Data: flow-automated-run-submission. API: group-runs, group-tokens.

Cross-feature: traceability and coverage

Story → AC → ATC → Test → Run → Bug is one chain read across five features. The traceability view (/projects/[slug]/traceability?story=) walks it for one story; metrics and workspace coverage aggregate it. A break anywhere (an ATC with no AC, a run whose ATC was deleted and is kept only as a snapshot, a bug without run) shows up here first, which makes this view a good oracle for end-to-end tests.

API endpoint inventory (pointers)

Endpoints live in business-api-context (bun run context:map business-api-context). Domain to group: auth → group-auth; workspaces → group-workspaces; members and invites → group-members-invites; projects and modules → group-projects-modules; stories and ACs → group-stories-ac; ATCs → group-atcs; tests → group-tests; runs → group-runs; bugs → group-bugs; plans and milestones → group-test-plans-milestones; environments → group-environments; tokens → group-tokens; billing → group-billing; Jira and imports → group-jira-imports; chat, notifications, activity, saved views, search → group-collaboration; metrics, coverage, traceability, heatmap → group-reports; export and deletion → group-data-lifecycle; admin and health → group-system.

Discovery gaps

  • Only one staging test account exists (STAGING_USER_EMAIL); no viewer, member or admin user, so role journeys cannot be automated yet.
  • I could not verify role gates on the members page, /settings/jira (calls notFound) and the tokens page beyond grep.
  • I could not verify the attachment upload endpoint, the runner's file-bug entry point, the milestone readiness endpoint, or the contents of metrics and heatmap pages.
  • Project name length, sign-in password minimum, token expiry server limits and environment URL validation were not found.
  • The data-export permission requirement was not found in the route posture scan.
  • Delete is absent from the API contract for projects, tests, test plans, milestones and bugs (public/openapi.json, 2026-11-10); server actions behind the UI were not traced, so a UI delete may still exist.
  • No separate coverage page was found; coverage is read through metrics and workspace coverage endpoints (inferred).
  • The legacy feature map and PRD journeys in the product repo were used as input only; they mark built features as planned.
